properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EXPAND OPER LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2/27/2026
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 8265639
Permit API: 015-23981
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Wysox Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2/27/2026
Comments: On 02/26/2025 Expand representative Steven Moyer reported a discovered release onsite. He stated "there was a hole in containment. They picked up the containment around 1100 hours that morning. An unknown amount of frack water mixed with stormwater on pad. Creston Environmental will be conducting the cleanup." On 02/27/2026 the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident response inspection of the Wygrala Well Pad in Wysox Township, Bradford County. The weather was 30 degrees and sunny. I arrived at 0915 hours. Upon arrival to the site DEP met with Expand representative Danielle Schadd and two Creston Environmental representatives. The area of the reported release is estimated to be an area of 75x150. There were barricades in place to keep the area closed off to vehicles (photo #2). Within the 75x150 area the elevated conductivity of the soil varies between 0-4 mS/cm. There were no pooled fluids within the reported release area. Approximately 2-3 inches of material had already been excavated and placed into containment onsite. Alderdice, Inc. was onsite removing the material during the inspection. Creston Environmental was conducting further testing during the inspection. They were going to expand their testing area due to the ground thawing with increased temperatures. The cause of the release was due to a ripped seam in the pad wide containment. This caused freshwater and brine mixture to leak through onto the pad surface. The same pad wide containment was in place during stimulation (01/23/2026-02/12/2926) and drill out (02/15/2026-02/18/2026). The quantity of the release is unknown. Due to the unknown quantity of the release this is being referred to ECB for Act 2 compliance.Based on the reported release (CTS #395411) the following violations have been cited against API #015-23981:CSL 402(b)35 P.S. 6018.301 SWMA25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a)I departed at 1000 hours.

Report Details

Violation Code: 78a53 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL AND STORMWATER MANAGEMENT - Person proposing or conducting earth disturbance activities associated with oil and gas operations failed to comply with 25 Pa. Code § 102.
Violation ID: 8259742
Permit API: 051-24303
Unconventional: Yes
County: Fayette
Municipality: Springfield Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 12/18/2025
Comments: On December 18, 2025, the Department conducted a follow-up inspection to IR 4106458 at the former location of the MAWC well site in Springfield Township, Fayette County. A violation that was issued in issued in IR 4084771 was left outstanding in IR 4106458, for failure to have a written restoration plan narrative onsite. The remaining violations issued in IR 4084771 were not left outstanding in IR 4106458, as they could not be evaluated due to the snow cover during the time of IR 4106458. The Department requested an NOV Response to IR 4084771 from the operator by December 4, 2025. However, no formal response to IR 4084771 has been received to-date from the operator.The First Modification to the COA was entered on May 1, 2025. Paragraph 3i of the 12/16/2021 CO and A states: "M4 shall immediately commence work to completely restore the Well sites upon execution of the First Amendment and complete restoration of the Well Sites by October 30, 2025, in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas act, 58 Pa.C.S. 3216, the site restoration regulations set forth in 25 Pa. Code 78a.65, and all applicable provisions of the Clean Streams Law and the regulations promulgated thereunder. M4 shall submit form 8000 PM-OOGN0075, "Well Site Restoration Report," within sixty (60) days of restoring the Well Sites."Site restoration is to be conducted "as closely to original conditions as practicable, including restoration of original contours and capability of supporting land uses existing prior to drilling of the Well(s) by October 30, 2025, unless M4 obtains a signed and notarized written consent of the landowner to leave the Well Site in an altered state".The following was observed:The Act 9 sign has been removed from the entrance of the pre-existing access road (photo 1). The access road is to remain unrestored, as it predates construction of the well site (photos 2-4). Temporary stabilization is inconsistent throughout the former well site, as large areas of exposed soil were observed on the slopes at the northern and southern site boundaries (photos 7, 8, 15, and 16). No loose sediment was observed in the rock-lined channels that empty into the pre-existing Sediment Trap (photos 9 and 12). Compost Filter Sock (CFS) is installed at the northern and southern boundaries (photos 9, 11, 17, and 19). The improperly installed super silt fence which was identified in IR 4084771 remains, with the fabric having completely detached and fallen to the ground (photo 18). No evidence of accelerated erosion and sedimentation was observed on site during this inspection. No restoration plans were found on site during this inspection.The Department continues to recommend that the operator reassess whether the E and S controls installed on site are adequate for this well site restoration.The Department also continues to recommend that the operator apply additional temporary stabilization where bare soil is exposed.Based on observations from this inspection, violations issued in IR 4084771 shall remain outstanding. An additional violation shall be issued against the lack of adequate temporary stabilization at the northern and southern site boundaries.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 9/15/2025 to PA MINERAL SVCS LLC in Unity Township, Westmoreland county. 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: PA MINERAL SVCS LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 9/15/2025
Violation Code: 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8249069
Permit API: 129-24019
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Unity Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/15/2025
Comments: On September 15 2025, the Department conducted an inspection of the E Shuster 2 OG Well in response to an OGI referral of the production tank leaking what appeared to be production fluid.At the time of inspection, the well appeared to drilled and equipped for production. The well tag was present on the well head. During the inspection, it appeared the production tank had previously been leaking and/or overflowed, but did not appear to be actively leaking. The tank appeared to be approximately 80% full at the time of the inspection.At the base of the production tank, there appeared to be an excess amount of fluid along with a thick oil based matter. There appeared to be absorbent mats on the ground next to and under the production tank where the release appeared to have occurred. Based on the amount of fluid on the ground observed by the Department, this appeared to be a reportable release (5 gallons or more). A background conductivity reading was taken and was 0.05mS. Conductivity readings were taken in the soil in the area of the spill. While some readings appeared comparable to the background reading, others were elevated in comparison to the background reading. Readings of 0.09mS 0.10mS, 0.14mS 0.31mS, 0.39mS, 0.41mS, 0.49ms, 0.64mS, 1.39mS, 1.33mS were obtained by the Department. Elevated readings were detected in about a 1 foot radius around the production tank.Prior to leaving the location, the Department contacted operator representative Joe Miller to inform him of the release. Mr. Miller indicated that they had replaced/repaired a faulty dump valve the week prior. He stated field members would be at the site to assess the area for a release and remediation would occur as necessary. The Department recommended that the Operator take immediate action to remediate the area in accordance with the Department's current spill policy.The operator is requested to submit a written response within 7 days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include:1.) An incident report including the quantity and type of fluid released (including the oil based matter) and how this was determined.2.) How long it is believed the release was occurring,3.) A timeline of remedial measures, and plan for remediation of the spill or release.4.) Clarification/waste manifests for any production fluid or other production waste that has been disposed of from the site in the last 2 years.The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the failure to properly control production fluid (and/or other fluids) resulting in a release to the ground, as well as failure to report a release.

Comments: On November 19 2025, the Department conducted a follow up inspection in regards to violations issued under inspection report 4065561. This gas well is currently under an Order (Enf ID 442909). This inspection is not evaluating the operator's compliance with the Order.At the time of the inspection, the well site appeared to remain unchanged. The Department again observed piping which ran to/from theproduction tank and the valve near the bottom of the tank, both of which appeared to be heavily corroded. The Department observed what appeared to be production fluid actively leaking from the piping onto the ground.The leak appeared to be a slow drip from the piping onto the ground. Department obtained a conductivity reading of the fluid on the pipe of 11.19mS. The Department obtained conductivity readings in the gravel below the corroded piping of 4.77ms, substantiating a release is still ongoing.The operator previously provided a response regarding the release on 10/2/2025 stating the following:"Our plan to correct this is as follows: Have brine hauled away, repair lines leading to tank, cause is just age, paint well, Schedule for completion of these repairs will depend on availably of hauling company. Well painting will need to be completed in accordance with weather conditions once other repairs are completed. we expect repairs should be completed within 90 days".Based on today's inspection, violations are outstanding.

Puddles observed on the pad surface in front of the production tanks had field measured conductivities of 2.9 - 3.61mS/cm. A puddle was observed in the drive lane east of the producing wells with a field measured conductivity of 2.76mS/cm. The 30HU - 34HU, 39HU and 78H wells were observed in production/flowback within secondary containment. Two additional wells drilled by the previous operator, the 22H and 24H wells were also observed capable of production. A narrow area on the western side of the well pad, where approximately 1.5' of the surface material had been removed, was observed holding puddles with a field conductivity of 2.78 - 4.32mS/cm. Stockpiles of material were observed on the support pad below the fill slope. A newly constructed PCSM basin was observed below the access road.Violations of the following regulations are cited as OUTSTANDING against the Cruttenden 846 34HU, API#117-22129 :SWMA 301 25 Pa Code 78a.56(a)The violation of CSL 402(b), originally cited 1/11/23 in IR#3486282 and 2/17/23 in IR#3506790. An operator response was received on 2/22/23 stating "Seneca denies the alleged violations set forth in the Departments referenced NOV issued 1/13/2023. However, as the Department collected samples (4427-295, 4427-296, 4427-297, and 4427-298) that were sent to the state laboratory for analysis, Seneca will provide a more detailed response to the Department once those sample results are made available." Samples results 4427-295,298 were provided to the Operator in an IR#3506790 dated 2/17/23. Please estimate the volume of pollutional material that was released to the pad surface. If the estimated volume is greater than or equal to 42 gallons, please include the information requested in. 25 Pa Code 78a.66(c)(2)(i).I departed the site at 1515 hours.

Comments: I conducted an Incident Response inspection of Diversified Production, LLC's Pickup Unit 1 well site (API 063-31495) in Green Twp., Indiana Co. This conventional well was drilled in July 1996 off Alder Road in Commodore, PA in a forested area.Diversified reported a brine release from the Pickup Unit 1 well site on 8/5/2024. A nipple rotted through a 100-barrel brine tank and approximately 12.5 barrels (525 gallons) was released onto the ground. The impacted area was approximately 8'x15'. Comments: On 7/15/2026, the Department conducted an inspection at the Schimizzi S and M 1 well site in Hempfield Township, Westmoreland County. This inspection follows up to IR 4187078, where violations were left outstanding due to no observable Act 9 sign and available Emergency Response plan (ERP) onsite. Since the time of IR 3484420, the soil conductivity onsite appeared to be comparable with that of the surrounding soil. Since the time of IR 3978494, no staining or distressed vegetation was observed around the production tanks.On 4/02/2026, Big Dog Energy representative responded via email to IR 4168852 and stated "As the DEP is aware this well was sold to Murphy Production in 2024. No staining or distressed vegetation was observed on the ground around the gas well (photos 1-3). The well postings onsite include contact information for Dorso LP (photo 6). Outstanding violations issued against the operator's posted information are being overseen by the OG SubSurface team. The additional piping and production equipment that does not appear to be in use remains onsite (photos 4 and 5). A violation was issued in IR 4170358 for failure to remove equipment that is not necessary for production, in accordance with in accordance with OGA3216(C).The well site overall exhibits greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. No accelerated erosion and sedimentation concerns are observed at this time (photos 1, 9, and 12).Based on observations from this inspection, violations that were continued in IR 4187078 remain outstanding, as it appears that no corrective action has been taken onsite since the date of that inspection and no formal NOV Response of any kind to IR 3093059 has been received to date.

Inspection Date: 10/18/2024
Comments: On October 18 2024 the Department conducted an inspection in regards to a spill reported under CTS 384608. Present during the inspection were operator representatives Paul Stiner and Bryan Goletz.The findings are as follows:Upon talking to the operator while onsite, it was stated that a check valve had broke causing a pressure build up to occur in the underground poly flow line, resulting in the line to fail. The failure in the poly line caused roughly 55 barrels of brine to be released into the ground. The release was observed by the operator at roughly 12 pm on 10/18/24, and reported to the Department at 1:17pm on 10/18/2024 . While onsite, the Department observed Penn Plus onsite beginning remediation efforts. According to Mr.Stiner, triaxle trucks are to arrive to the site on 10/21/2024, and all impacted soil would be excavated and disposed of. The operator stated because of the size of the release, they will be under going Act 2 remediation, with Moody preparing all of the related Act 2 documents/reports.Upon inspection of the location of the spill, the Department observed what appeared to be the location of the failure in the poly line (photos 1 and 2). A conductivity reading was taken in this location with a reading of "OR" (Out of range of maximum readings).The Department observed puddles of fluid on the surface of the well site (photos 5-7). The Department observed a tanker truck onsite using suction hoses to remove the excess fluid/puddles from the ground. Conductivity readings were taken with in the puddles as well as downslope from the location of the poly line failure with multiple readings of "OR". Elevated readings (9.22mS) were detected roughly 175 feet down slope (east) of the failure. Mr.Stiner stated he had obtained elevated readings approximately 180 feet from the poly line failure and the depth of contamination appeared to be roughly 2 feet (photo 14). No impacts to waters of the commonwealth were observed.The Department recommends the operator follows the Department's Spill Policy and October 3 2014 Program Clarification Memo for remediation of the spill. The Department requests the waste manifest for the impacted material upon receipt.The Operator is requested to submit a written response within 15 business days of the spill or release.This response should include an incident report, a timeline, the regulation substance involved, where the spill or release occur, the environmental media affected, any impacts to water supplies, buildings, or utilities, and interim actions planned, initiated, or completed.The Department is requesting how the operator quantified the amount spilled. Any new impacts discovered or identified during interim remedial actions or site characterization should also be reported to the Department within 15 calendar days of discovery.Within 180 days of the spill or release the operator must perform a site characterization to determine the extent and magnitude of the contamination and submit the site characterization report to the undersigned.Based on todays inspection, violations are being issued for the observed release.

Present during today's inspection were operator representative Jay Niehenke and Ronald Seich.The findings are as follows:According to Mr. Seich and Mr. Niehenke, excavation was completed on 3/26/2025 and Moody was onsite that same day to conduct a site investigation and collect samples for Act 2 remediation.The Department's findings are as follows:At the time of the inspection, it appears additional excavation has occurred. It appears additional material has been excavated in the ditch up to the northern and southern booms as well as around the production equipment. There appeared to be a large amount of excavation where the production tank previously was, with excavation appearing reach approximately 4 feet deep. Conductivity readings were taken in the area of excavation around the production equipment and where the production tank previously was with readings of 0.08mS, 0.16mS, and 0.51mS. These readings appear to be comparable to the background conductivity reading obtained of 0.16mS. The Department recommends the operator promptly install/implement temporary erosion and sediment controls. The Department also recommends the operator temporarily stabilize any disturbed areas with in 4 days following cessation of earth disturbance activities. Based on today's inspection, violation remain outstanding as a notice of intent to conduct Act 2 remediation has not yet been received by the Department.

Violation ID: 862271

Unconventional: No

Inspection Date: 2019-09-16
Comments: This inspection was performed in response to a report, by the Operator, of a small release of crude oil along Irvine Run, in Brokenstraw Township, Warren County, PA. This is the second release to have occurred in association with this well this year. Please reference inspection ID#: 2870841. I was contacted by Rick Engelbert with Irvine Run Resources on September 13, 2019 to report the release of an unknown volume of crude oil to the ground along Irvine Run. The spill was reported to have been contained and was actively being cleaned up. A site visit was arranged for September 16, 2019. Legree 30, (37-123-26419): I met with Rick Engelbert on site at approximately 10:30 on September 16, 2019 to conduct an site investigation. Rick indicated that the well was pumped on August 31, 2019. A strong odor was noticed near the well on September 1st. A small amount of oil was found to have been seeping from the ground surface at the base of a hill side some ways below the well location;(At a similar elevation as the spill that occurred in April but further down on Irvine Run). A syphon dam was constructed below the area that was seeping oil. Absorbent materials were applied periodically to absorb the oil. A boom and some straw bails were placed in the stream channel of Irvine Run as a precautionary measure. Very little oil was believed to have made it into the stream. A leak test was performed on the buried lead line system that services the well. A small hole was found in a portion of the line near the well. The excavation exposing the line was still open while I was on site. All of the contaminated soil appeared to have been removed from the hole. Similar to the excavation created to expose the last leak associated with this well, the soil that was excavated didn't seem to have much oil contamination. Heavy rain in the last week apparently caused the volume of oil draining from the seep to increase. It was at this point that Rick contacted me to report the spill. Approximately ten gallons of oil is reported to have been gather up. I noticed a slight emulsion on the surface of the water behind the syphon dam while I was on site. The spill appears to be getting managed appropriately at this point. The operator indicated the absorbent materials will continue to be changed as needed. It has been advised to the operator that recoverable waste materials, including the contaminated soil that was excavated around the leak, be collected and disposed of at a land fill. A receipt of disposal should be sent to the Warren District Office upon disposal. The clean up progress will continue to be monitored with future inspections.

Comments: Arrived onsite in response to a reported release of approximately 32 gallons of high conductivity fluid. While removing containment after completing the frack a puddle was noticed and was determined to have elevated conductivity. I spoke with Mike Deming onsite. At the time of inspection, it was estimated that the total release was potentially more than 1 barrel and therefore Act 2 remediation would be pursued.The impacted area is on the southern side of the pad about 75' from the southern pad edge and 25' from the eastern pad edge. The scraped area was about 18' wide by 140' long and a few inches deep. Near a freshwater storage tank there was a puddle that had a conductivity greater than 4.00 millisiemens per centimeter (mS/cm). The puddle will be removed and after the tank is removed any necessary additional scraping will be performed. When possible, the rest of the containment will be removed to screen and scrape as needed.The pad beyond the visible impacted area was dry. The eastern side of the pad runs into the rock-lined cut slope. The southern and western sides of the pad lead into the PCSM. There were no seeps noted in the downslope areas and soil conductivities were at or below 0.02 mS/cm.

Comments: On 02/03/2025 a representative from the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a routine inspection of Greylock Production LLC's Ron multi-well pad located in Hector Township, Potter County. Upon arrival to the site at 0915 hours, weather was 33F and cloudy. An Act 9 sign is visible and located at the site entrance (photo #1).All standing water observed on the pad surface was frozen solid.There are 2 recently drilled wells located onsite which are currently undergoing flow back as a result of the completion of hydraulic fracturing activities; well permits are posted with the Act 9 sign at the site entrance (photos #1 and 2). 2 gas processing units (GPUs) are also located onsite (photo #3). The GPUs are not yet in use but are held in a secondary containment structure. There are 4 produced fluid tanks located onsite and stationed in secondary containment (photo #4); the tanks are not yet labeled, and I discussed the need to label them with personnel onsite; they informed me that they would be labeled after they dried off. Two modular aboveground storage structures (MASS's) are located onsite to hold brine during flow back, and a lined residual waste container is located next to them and held on containment (photo #5). Multiple upright brine and temporary storage tanks for holding produced fluids during flow back are also noted onsite; all tanks are held in secondary containment which appears to be functioning as intended (photos #6 and 7).Site stabilization could not be adequately assessed due to snow coverage. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation was observed. A weekly erosion and sediment (E and S) inspection log is available for review at the site entrance and is up to date (photo #8). One infiltration basin serve as the site's post construction stormwater management (PCSM) controls (photo #9). No standing water was observed in the PCSM control it appears to be functioning as intended.The violations noted in inspection report #'s 3881391 and 3878285 remain outstanding against API #105-21962.No violations noted. I departed the site at 1015 hours.

Comments: On 03/12/2024, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Morris F25 well site following violations issued on 12/19/2023 (IR 3662363, Enforcement 423308). I was accompanied by PA DEP Compliance Specialist, George Traister. Violations of 78.54, SWMA 301, 78.57(a), 91.34(a), and 78.66(b) were issued on 12/19/2023. The violations were issued as outstanding on 01/31/2024 (IR 3704581).The following was observed on 03/12/2024:Conductivity readings were taken within the water and gravel in the tank battery. The valve on Tank 1 looked to be leaking fluid. Crystallization was noted on the valve (Photo 1). The water within the battery around Tank 1 did not display elevated readings (Photo 2). The fluid escaping from the valve is recommended to be addressed. A reading was obtained within the gravel around the pan of Tank 4. This reading was 4.28 mS (Photo 3).Readings were taken within the gravel in the battery around Tank 5 and within the fluid in the pan. The readings within the gravel were 4.76 mS and 4.26 mS (Photos 4, 5). The reading within the pan was 17.30 mS (Photos 6, 7), which may indicate fluids leaking from tank fluid removal or from the valve itself. I recommend that this is addressed. The piping on the drain from the battery has been shortened. The exterior end is capped, and no elevated conductivity was noted on the ground below. The interior end is open, and I recommend that this is also capped. The water level in the battery is close to the edge of the pipe (Photos 8, 9). Stabilization has been added to the earthen berm. I recommend that additional is added as needed (Photos 10, 11).Pans are under each tank valve (Photo 12).Wet spots were noted on the exterior of the earthen berm. Conductivity readings were taken within these noted areas and resulted in the following: 4.00 mS, 6.33 mS, 5.44 mS. Another reading resulted in 1.15 mS. I recommend that fluid from inside the battery is not migrate through the berm. Livestock activity in the vicinity is taken into consideration (Photos 13-17). The violations issued on 12/29/2023 and 01/31/2024 remain outstanding.

Unconventional: No

Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/14/2024
Comments: On June 14, 2024 the Department conducted a Routine Inspection of the Joseph A Negri 1 well located in East Huntington Township, Westmoreland County. During a previous inspection (IR 3723492) the Department observed a drum on site with a Methanol label on it. At that time the Department requested the operator provide information by 3/29/24 on what exactly is in the drum and what it is being used for, the Department also requested that the Operator remove all equipment not necessary for production. The Department has not received a response from the Operator in regards to this site.At the time of this inspection, the well site was exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth with no accelerated erosion or sedimentation issues observed. A well tag with all required information posted on it was fixed to the wellhead. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near the wellhead. Some production equipment onsite that appeared to be in production due to the gauge attached to it had an open pipe close to the ground. A soil conductivity reading was taken at the edge of the well site in some vegetation as a background (0.0074 mS) and then a reading was taken directly next to the piping (0.409 mS) and then a little further back from this piping (0.382 mS). The production tank also had some wet marks coming from the top of the tank and the wet marks can be seen going down the tank towards the ground in areas. Soil conductivity readings were taken at the base of the production tank below areas where the wet marks were observed on the tank (0.1483 mS and 0.1405 mS). The drum of methanol was observed to still be on site, not in secondary containment and fluid can be seen sitting at the top of it with air bubbles forming from what may be a small hole or crack in the top of the barrel. Soil conductivity readings were taken at the base of the drum (0.096 mS), as well as in the fluid sitting at the top of the drum (0.620 mS).The soil conductivity readings taken near the open pipe and at the base of the production tank are elevated in comparison to the background soil conductivity reading and subjugate that there is some sort of release contaminating the soil in both areas. The reading at the base of the Methanol drum is comparable to the background, but the fluid sitting at the top and the air bubbles seen indicate that there may be a leak at the top of the drum which currently has the potential to reach the ground. While onsite, the Department spoke with Dave Lindahl of Mountain View to let him know about the elevated readings by the production equipment and production tank and informed him about the possible hole at the top of the Methanol Drum. The Department recommended the drum be removed or put in secondary containment as soon as possible and recommended they determine how the two leaks occurred, stop them, remove all contaminated soil, replace it with new top soil, and seed/mulch. Dave stated that someone would be onsite on 6/17/24 to begin working on all of this. The Department is recommending the Operator either remove this drum or put it within secondary containment by COB June 28, 2024. Based on todays inspection, violations shall be issued at this time for failure to remove production equipment not currently in use and for a release from production equipment.

Comments: On September 2, 2026, the Department conducted a follow up inspection in regards to violations issued under inspection report 4261627.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspection, the Department did not observe an Act 9 sign. The Department recommends the operator install an Act 9 sign in accordance with 78a55. The Department also did not observe an Emergency Response Plan (ERP). The Department recommends the operator ensure an ERP is onsite in accordance with 78a55.Upon inspection of the well site, the 2 previously observed corroded production tanks were still present onsite. While the Department did not observe any active leaks at the time of this inspection, the Department observed orange staining and saturated dirt/gravel surrounding the corroded tank. Elevated soil conductivity readings were again obtained around the corroded production tank. Conductivity readings of 5.11ms, 6.24mS, 6.68mS, and OR (Over detectable range, >20mS). Prior to leaving the site, the Department spoke with operator representative Robert Inghram and inquired if there was a timeline for removal of the tanks and remediation of the impacted soil. Mr. Inghram stated that the NOV (IR 4261627) was received and an NOV response was being prepared to be submitted to the Department. With the preparation of the NOV response, the operator is finalizing a contractor to conduct the work and work would begin as soon as they can get it scheduled.Based on today's inspection, violations for the observed release, production equipment onsite not in use, no ERP onsite, and no Act 9 Sign onsite remain outstanding.

properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Chevron Appalachia Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-12-05
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 870824
Permit API: 129-28979
Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: South Huntingdon Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-12-05
Comments: The inspection is being conducted in response to a spill reported by Chevron on 12/5/2019 at 10:30AM. According to the initial spill report, greater than 5 gallons of oil-based drilling mud was found under secondary containment upon removal of said containment. Removal of secondary containment is currently underway at the time of inspection. Chevron representative Curtis Small is on site. The Act 9 sign is present at the site entrance. The ERP, PPC, ESCGP approval, site plans, and drill permits are in the mailbox. No inspection logs or worksheets are present on site. Secondary containment inspections and repair records were requested from Curtis Small; he stated that the logs were not on site. Drilling mud and staining is present in multiple locations on the well pad (Photos #6, 7, 8, and 10) evidencing multiple breaches of secondary containment in multiple locations on the pad thereby strongly suggesting the drilling mud spill was substantial and widespread. Drilling mud has mixed with stormwater and has collected in puddles over greater than half the pad area (Photos # 9, 11, and 13). Multiple water puddles have a strong petroleum odor and have a greasy consistency, especially the dark areas at puddle edges (Photos #11 and 13). The contaminated stormwater has likely left the pad in multiple places and entered stormwater features and diversion channels. An unknown quantity of material has also been spilled near the pad entrance (Photos #2 and 3). Individual material particles are readily visible with the naked eye, coarse, and appear to be predominately silica. The Department requests the information on the material. The SW corner of the pad contains significant quantities of sediment and tire ruts (Photos #4 and 5). Multiple pieces of equipment currently not in use and lacking secondary containment are scattered around the well pad (Photos #1, 11, 12, and 13).
